assumptions: Pulse: sech2, transform limited, 850 fs. The pair (850 fs, 1.6 nm) has a time-bandwidth product of 0.38, below the Gaussian 0.44 and above the sech2 0.315, so no ideal shape satisfies both; the sech2 gives 1.1-1.3 nm. Bandwidth ratios are quoted against the paper's 1.6 nm and against ours.

Effective ROC 350 mm and the lens of the AR concave face are lumped into a thin mirror in air after the 26 mm of glass; the mirror distance 540 mm is the air gap; the start beam is the mode of the EMPTY 540 mm cell (459 um). The substrate/meniscus lens is not modelled separately.

The 91 % transmission is an input: the loss (mirror reflectance 0.91^(1/36)) is spread evenly over the bounces. In and out coupling prisms are not modelled. Energy is set from the output power: E_in = P_out / 0.91 / 10 MHz.
Air is included (Kerr, no rotational Raman) although the paper does not say whether the cell was evacuated; it contributes 0.1 rad of 17.4 rad.
Kerr and thermal lensing are inside the radial model only as far as the Kerr effect goes; no thermal lens, no M2 comparison, no mode-matching re-optimisation at each power.
